answer: A proof produced for one use is bound to that use by a challenge the prover could not have anticipated when it was created, so the work cannot be computed once and replayed across a fleet, and every use demands a fresh unpredictable input. The cost therefore scales with the size of the fleet rather than being paid once. Every use pulls a kernel, signs a relic against it, and the raven guarantees the relic was not ready in advance: the fleet can copy keys but never a kernel it did not receive in the moment. Recording and replaying is exactly what the challenge defeats.
